free_text: The patient is a 61-year-old male with a PSA of 3.9 and a biopsy-confirmed Gleason 3+5 (ISUP Grade Group 4) prostate adenocarcinoma with perineural invasion. MRI demonstrated a PI-RADS 5 lesion with extracapsular extension features, classifying the clinical T stage as cT3. The management assessment is to review individual treatment benefit and patient preferences, balancing potential treatment efficacy against risks.
